name: Fed Policy Pack
description: Zscaler's Fed Policy Pack V1.1 plus the CUI Marking design: dictionaries, engines and monitor rules for FOUO markings, Atomic Energy Act RD/FRD, Standard Forms, US PII, US PHI, financial information, ITAR, Traffic Light Protocol and private keys, and Controlled Unclassified Information by its markings (31 dictionaries in seven tiers: structural banners and portion marks, category tokens, malformed-marking proximity, legacy FOUO/LES/SBU/distribution statements, designation blocks, a decontrol exclusion and contextual vocabulary) behind block, caution and monitor rules. Every rule is mirrored to Endpoint, SaaS and Email DLP. All rules ship DISABLED at INFO severity (Zscaler's delivery convention): review, tune, then enable each rule and raise its severity.
deploy_note: INSTALL ONE CHANNEL AT A TIME. Deploy Web DLP first, check it, then Endpoint DLP, then SaaS, then Email, one channel per run. A small run is easy to verify and avoids the burst of requests that makes ZIA block the API client (Resource Access Blocked).
references: NARA CUI Registry and CUI Marking Handbook
audience: US federal civilian agencies, the defense industrial base and federal contractors handling CUI (32 CFR 2002, NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC), FOUO, Atomic Energy Act data, ITAR, and US PII/PHI.
when_to_use: The customer is a federal agency or contractor, or marks documents with CUI banners, portion marks or category codes (SP-CTI, PRVCY, ...), or still has legacy FOUO/LES/SBU material. It is a superset of the ZBP Enterprise baseline; do not deploy both.
notes: CUI detection is generated from cui_design.json (the ZIA dlpDictionaries design with _tier/_intended_action/_min_match_count metadata) with: python tools/pack_from_design.py fed_policy_pack. It replaces the V1.1 'CUI Engine (High/Medium/Low Confidence)' engines and their eight dictionaries; the V1.1 contextual phrases, category names and declassify-date patterns live on as tier 7 and CUI-Declassify-Date.
The V1.1 'AEA Medium Confidence' engine was attached to no rule and is not shipped; 'Z-Atomic Energy Act Monitor' uses AEA High Confidence.

FOUO is detected twice on purpose: 'Z-For Official Use Only Markings-Monitor' (typo-tolerant, two confidence levels) and Legacy-FOUO inside the block-grade CUI engine. ZIA applies the first matching rule in order, so place the FOUO monitor rule above CUI-Monitor-Marked-Documents while you tune.
Multi-word phrases are quoted ("FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY") because ZIA phrases fuzzy-match unless quoted; single tokens (NOFORN, POC) are left bare.
Engine expressions are the API form: ((Dn.S > 0) OR ...) AND NOT (Dm.S > 0); .S sums match counts. Per-dictionary minimum counts live in the engine (> 1 means at least two matches).

Engine Builder limits: max 4 subexpressions and 4 operators per level, 16 dictionaries per operator; Exclude must sit in a subexpression. CUI-Detect-All uses two nested OR groups solely for the 16-dictionary ceiling. Validate that the nesting renders in the portal's Engine Builder; if it is rejected, restructure as a root OR over the two groups and repeat the decontrol exclusion in each.

Proximity measures between a PATTERN and a PHRASE inside a custom dictionary; pattern-to-pattern proximity does not exist. Tier 3 (CUI-Prox-*) and CUI-Designation-Indicator therefore use MATCH_CUSTOM_ANY_PATTERN_WITH_ANY_PHRASE with the CUI token as the pattern anchor and the category code or field labels as phrases, with proximityEnabledForCustomDictionary set (ZIA needs both the window and the flag). Windows are bidirectional bytes over extracted text, so OOXML part boundaries inflate distance.

Phrase matching is always case-insensitive and ignores punctuation; quotes only force exact word order and disable noise-word tolerance. The phrase SP-EXPT therefore also matches lowercase and hyphen-absent variants; the CUI pattern anchor is what keeps tier 3 precise. Phrases are 3-128 bytes, at most 256 per dictionary; engine match counts must be under 1000.

CUI-Basic-Bare is the highest-volume, lowest-precision dictionary (min 3 at the engine). The design note asks for Count Unique; the design file ships PATTERN_COUNT_TYPE_ALL, so switch the pattern action to PATTERN_COUNT_TYPE_UNIQUE in design.json if repeated 'CUI' tokens over-count. It is wired only to the caution and monitor engines; never to block.
Bare LES is deliberately excluded from Legacy-LES (collides with French text, surnames and unrelated acronyms); only the spelled form or banner context matches.
CUI-Decontrol-Context is a document-scoped exclusion: a genuine CUI document that cites its own marking guide is suppressed. Record this in the residual-risk statement.

Documented limits enforced at preflight: 8 patterns per dictionary, 256 bytes per pattern, proximity 0-10000 bytes, no lookaround. Proximity windows (300-600 bytes) are bidirectional over extracted text and unreliable for spreadsheets, multi-column PDFs and OCR output.
Deploy order for a customer: enable CUI-Monitor-All and the Z-*-Monitor rules; review incidents for a week; then CUI-Monitor-Marked-Documents, then CUI-Monitor-Weak-Markings.

Every rule ships DISABLED and monitor-only (ALLOW, or report incident on SaaS). Nothing in the pack blocks; enforcing a rule is the customer's decision in the portal once incidents have been reviewed, and the journey records it as progress.
